newsitem.title: USA: Castle & Cooke sees ongoing negative effects.
newsitem.headline: Castle & Cooke sees ongoing negative effects.

text.p: Castle & Cooke Inc said on Monday the soft Hawaii economy continues to have an adverse impact its residential operations and will have a negative effect on operating results in 1997.

Castle and Cooke posted fourth-quarter profits of $200,000, or $0.01 a share, compared with $9.4 million, or $0.47 a share in the year ago period. Revenues for the fourth quarter were $91.7 million compared with $115.8 million in the year-ago period.
"The soft Hawaii economy continues to have an adverse impact on our residential operations," said David Murdock, chairman and chief executive.

"We continue to focus our efforts on marketing and inventory management in this difficult economic environment, but expect that this challenging market will continue to have a negative effect on our operating results in 1997," he said.
Murdock said the company is looking at acquisition opportunities in mainland markets to further growth.

Castle & Cooke is a residential real estate developer in Hawaii, California and Arizona. It also owns and operates two of resorts on the island of Lana'i in Hawaii and is involved in commercial development in Hawaii, California, Arizona, North Carolina and Georgia.
